author: Michelle Wiles | Brand Futures
title: you don't need taste, you need creative direction
text:
you don’t need taste, you need creative direction
Good taste is the floor
It feels like every week there’s another post that declares taste the driver of value in a post-AI world. The logic is that since AI allows people to create as much content as they want, value will come from curation of said content.
Taste matters. It just isn’t the thing that wins.
Yes, there is value in great curation. If you are an editor at a magazine or a buyer at a department store, then yes, taste is everything. But for those jobs, it always has been.
The problem with taste for brand leaders is that it assumes that the best ideas are lying around and waiting for someone to pick them. But that’s not true. Even for the most basic form of AI content creator — a chatbot — you still have to input the right prompt in order to get something out that’s good. In other words: you need to have a vision for what you want before you begin curating or applying your ‘taste’ to the world.
Great brand campaigns and products will not come from curating a set of existing possibilities into something good. Especially when everyone now has access to those same possibilities. The leading brands blaze a new path by creating a new world consumers want to be a part of.
Take Bandit, one of the fastest growing sportswear brands. Bandit’s New York aesthetic, its viral marketing initiatives, and its innovative products are all new and fresh on the market. They might be inspired by other domains, but the output is the work of a team delivering a sharp point of view on running gear. Bandit isn’t curating. It’s creating.
Or Liquid Death, a brand that manages to sell water at high volumes at a massive markup and consistently go viral online on the strength of its packaging, its energy-drink positioning, and its out-there content. Liquid Death didn’t curate an aesthetic, it created an entirely new one.
Or Chanel, one of the few brands defying the slump in luxury sales. Chanel is not winning because Chanel has the best taste. Chanel is winning because Chanel empowered their creative director to put together a fresh new world of shows and products and campaigns that feel aspirational to be a part of.
Yes, taste is part of all of these brands. But the strongest brands add on something new. That takes forward-thinking creative direction and a team with a license to stand out from what is currently considered “good taste” by the market.
If anything, the flood of AI content widens the opening for people willing to break from the crowd. Aesthetics spread faster now. Trends normalise in weeks. It’s easier than ever to have ‘good taste’ because influencers distribute it in real time. Work that breaks from the pack reads as fresh precisely because everything around it has started to blur together.
The creation of something new — not recommending an A24 movie, but directing one — that’s where the value will be.
